newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - FTSE call spreads traded as market weakens.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FTSE call spreads traded as market weakens.

text.p: A call spread in the FTSE 100 index was the main equity options deal on Monday as the stock market eased back, dealers said.

Part of the original spread was crossed. The original deal was the sale of 3,000 March 4300 calls at 73p and the purchase of 3,000 March 4400 calls at 27p for a net credit of 46p. A local, or independent trader bought 2,000 lots in the crossed trade.
For a profit, the seller of the spread requires the value of the spread to reduce and for maximum profit that both options expire worthless which will happen if the FTSE falls below 4300.
But dealers believe the position may have been hedged by buying FTSE futures so that for a profit, market volatility needs to fall as this will reduce the value of the options.
In contrast, the buyer of the spread requires the market to move above 4400 by March expiry so that a maximum 54p profit can be realised.
And if this long spread was hedged by selling futures then increased market volatility will help it turn in a profit.
By 1545 GMT, spot FTSE was down 9.3 at 4331.7 while March futures had shed eight points to 4324.
Over in stock options, British Gas was busy.
British Gas was demerged into a new company called Centrica -- which now sells gas to consumers -- and BG -- responsible for pipelines and exploration and production.
For the purposes of traded options the combined share prices of Centrica and BG gives the underlying price in what was formerly British Gas.

The main deal in British Gas was a split synthetic from the sale of 1,000 March 240 calls at 8-1/2p and the purchase of 1,000 March 220 puts at 2p. Centrica shares fell 10-1/4p to 65-1/4p while those for BG went up 3p to 173-1/2p.
